text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Traffic experts, concerned about speeding and flouting of road rules, call for speed cameras to be installed at traffic lights.

- Malta Drydocks must regain lost credibility, Prime Minister Alfred Sant says, adding that dockyard could not continue paying for overtime which was not justified. Dockyard workers last week held protests calling for the removal of the government-appointed chairman, blaming him for a drop in orders. Chairman Noel Zarb Adami has said he has no intention of stepping down.
- Man charged with drug trafficking, money laundering and possession of guns and ammunition. The 35-year-old father of five was arrested at his house after allegedly selling heroin.
- Summer starts with music, says paper, publishing a half-page picture of disco-party held by the opposition Nationalist Party.
